client_brief:
Distillery mark recovery and a matching set of packaging photographs

This is a focused identity-production commission for Coble & Vane. We need the existing mark recovered in colour, as a supporting preview, and in true one-ink form, alongside our three packaging photographs, of the neck seal, the crate end and the cap top, which currently disagree because of their lighting: the supplier sheet shows each one beside the version applied there, all three brought to one neutral light.

The commission

 One-colour packaging identity: 1 named export. The mark uses the one-ink treatment our suppliers ask for in supplier_emails.txt. The counter spaces remain open on the neck seal, at the seal size the supplier sheet states and shows at actual size.

 Cask-release label artwork: 8 named exports. The release details match this record: the label carries our recovered one-ink mark, the cask's photograph, and its expression name, cask number, strength, outturn, filling date, bottling date, volume and distilled-at line, each written as the record writes it, with the expression name, set in our display face, as its largest line, above the cask number and strength. Last season's tasting note does not carry over, and the label claims nothing beyond what this record and our brand identity support. The label respects the supplied packaging area.

 Packaging supplier application sheet: 1 named export. The ink treatment is unambiguous: for the neck seal, the crate end and the cap top, the sheet names the version that item's supplier receives and the one ink or finish it is applied in. The application scale is stated: the size of the mark on the neck seal, the crate end and the cap top, taking a supplier's own figure wherever one is given.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: A two-person coastal distillery making small-batch gin and cask-strength single malt, sold shop-direct and through independent merchants.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2020, on the Northumberland coast, England. A two-person distillery: Iris runs the still, her partner runs everything else.
brand_identity.about: Coble & Vane is a working distillery on a stretch of the North Sea coast, named for the flat-bottomed fishing boat that once beached below the still house. We release twelve casks a year and nothing we cannot stand behind. The bottle is meant to earn its place on a shelf and in a hand, not to shout across the shop.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged 30 to 55 choosing a gift or a considered bottle, and the independent merchant deciding whether the bottle earns its shelf facing. People who read a label closely and reward restraint.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Bottles 55 to 120 dollars: standard gin at 55, cask-strength single malt from 95 to 120. Upper-craft tier, sitting deliberately apart from the twelve-dollar shelf. Value is carried by finish, emboss and wax rather than by loud print.

palette.name: Deep Sea Iron
palette.role: mandatory on the labels and the supplier sheet
palette.usage: The one deep ink: expression names, the wordmark, cask numbers, strengths, dates, body text and headings, as on cask_labels_2025_PRINT.pdf, and the mark wherever it is printed on a label.

palette.name: Oxblood Wax
palette.role: mandatory wherever the wordmark is set
palette.usage: The 0.75 pt hairline 1.5 mm beneath the wordmark, and rules, as on cask_labels_2025_PRINT.pdf. Never a ground, a panel, body text or the mark; on the supplier sheet it may also fill a small swatch naming an item's ink or finish.

palette.name: Cold Slate
palette.usage: Small field labels such as CASK NO. and STRENGTH, and the legal line, as on cask_labels_2025_PRINT.pdf. Never a ground, a panel, body text or the mark; on the supplier sheet it may also fill a small swatch naming an item's ink or finish.

palette.name: Bleached Rope
palette.usage: The ground of the whole label sheet, as on cask_labels_2025_PRINT.pdf, and the only colour a ground or panel on the supplier sheet may take, apart from a small swatch naming an item's ink or finish. Never type.

palette.name: Coble Black
palette.usage: The single solid fill of one-ink-mark.svg, the black-on-transparent art supplier_emails.txt asks for, and that mark and the versions drawn from it wherever the supplier sheet shows them as supplied, or a small swatch naming an item's ink. Never type, and never on a label, where Deep Sea Iron is the one deep ink.

brand_identity.typography: Coble & Vane runs two families. Step 01 is the wordmark in Mercury Display Roman, caps at 22 pt on 24 pt tracked to 200 units and never below, with a 0.75 pt Oxblood Wax hairline cut to the exact optical width of that letterspaced line sitting 1.5 mm beneath it. Step 02 is cask number and strength in National 2 Medium at 14 pt on 17 pt with tracking at +25 units, always tabular lining figures so a case of bottles lines up digit under digit; the existing prose assigns this role to the text family rather than to Mercury, so it stays there. Step 03 is body in National 2 Regular at 8 pt on 11 pt, tracking 0 units, measure held to a maximum of 65 characters, with supplier sheets at 9.5 pt on 13 pt instead. Step 04 is legal in the same face at 6 pt on 8.5 pt with tracking at +12 units. One deep ink, plenty of air, and nothing shiny.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, dry, unhurried. Written as instruction, not advertisement. Example line: "One ink, plenty of air, and nothing shiny. If our own list looks wrong to you, say so before you make it."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The house mark was drawn six years ago by an illustrator who has since moved abroad and cannot be reached. It survives only as a full-colour illustration flattened to a single PNG. There are no vector files, no one-ink versions, and no supplier guidance sheet. Every single-colour version a supplier has ever received was improvised from that one file, and no two have matched.
brand_identity.values: Restraint and honesty. One deep ink, generous clear space, and finishes that carry the value instead of the print. Say plainly what a version can and cannot do.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: The wordmark is Mercury Display Roman caps tracked to 200 units with a 0.75 pt Oxblood Wax hairline cut to the exact optical width of that letterspaced line sitting 1.5 mm below it.

scale.note: The wordmark. Caps, tracked to 200 units and never below. A 0.75 pt Oxblood Wax hairline, cut to the exact optical width of that letterspaced line, sits 1.5 mm beneath it. Size and tracking both come from the existing prose; only the leading is added.

Cask number and strength, set in tabular lining figures so every bottle in a case lines up digit under digit. The existing prose assigns this role to National 2 Medium at 14 pt rather than to the display face, so the text family carries step 02 here.

scale.sample: Twelve casks a year and nothing we cannot stand behind.
scale.note: Both numbers already stated in the existing prose. Supplier sheets set the same face and leading relationship at 9.5 pt on 13 pt.

scale.sample: 700ml · Distilled and bottled on the Northumberland coast.
scale.note: Legal. 6 pt comes from the existing prose; leading and the slight positive tracking are added so it survives one deep ink on an uncoated label.

type_system.signature_move: The wordmark is Mercury Display Roman caps at 22 pt tracked to 200 units with a 0.75 pt Oxblood Wax hairline cut to the exact optical width of that letterspaced line sitting 1.5 mm below it. Step 01 carries the tracked bar and the hairline, and tabular lining figures at step 02 keep the second half of the house behaviour visible.
rules: Never track the wordmark below 200 units.
The 0.75 pt Oxblood Wax hairline is cut to the exact optical width of the letterspaced wordmark and sits 1.5 mm beneath it, never a standard rule width.
Cask number and strength are always National 2 Medium tabular lining figures so columns align across a case.
Supplier sheets set body at 9.5 pt rather than 8 pt. No other body size exists.
One deep ink, generous clear space and nothing shiny. Value is carried by finish, emboss and wax, never by louder print.
Say plainly what a version can and cannot do. The type sheet is written as instruction, not as advertisement.

palette_rules.distribution: On every label the ground is Bleached Rope; expression names, the wordmark, values, body text and the mark are Deep Sea Iron, the one deep ink; Cold Slate is for small field labels and the legal line; Oxblood Wax is for the wordmark hairline and rules, as on cask_labels_2025_PRINT.pdf. The supplier sheet keeps the same pairings on Bleached Rope or the unprinted page, shows one-ink-mark.svg and the versions drawn from it in Coble Black as supplied, and may show the ink or finish an item is applied in as a small swatch. Cold Slate and Oxblood Wax together stay under 5% of the designed, non-photographic area of any label or page, and are never a ground.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity, in the mark, on the labels and on the supplier sheet: no tint, screen, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, laid over a photograph.
palette_rules.forbidden: Nothing shiny: no gold, silver, bronze, copper, foil, metallic or gloss effect on any type, rule, mark, panel or icon. No second deep ink beside Deep Sea Iron on a label, and no colour outside the five palette hexes for type, panels, rules, the mark or icons.
palette_rules.photography: Photographs keep their own corrected colour and are never recoloured toward the palette. cv_packaging_wax_seal.jpg, cv_packaging_crate_end.jpg and cv_packaging_cap_top.jpg are brought to one neutral light, and the wax in cv_packaging_wax_seal.jpg keeps its photographed texture and is not replaced by a flat fill. Each cask photograph keeps the colour of its spirit as shot.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
